correctness.rationale: The invertible transverse-normal coordinate map has determinant sin(beta), yielding the exact rectangular-slice integral for volume. Coarea first variation identifies the two radius derivatives with exposed Euclidean cylindrical surface patches; Euler homogeneity yields Q=3-(t-1)F′/F. The ratio decreases strictly because the pointwise derivative of g_t is positive and its covariance with the density score is nonnegative. Direct endpoint singular integral gives F″=-4log(1/eta)+O(1), hence the 3/4 logarithm. Uniform large-t binomial expansion yields the stated second-order coefficient. A fresh checker independently tested 123 finite diagnostics including elliptical formulas. Proof, not finite tests, supports all quantifiers.

value.rationale: The ratio rS/V is a dimensionless geometric efficiency observable for a real intersecting-pipe family. A strict global shape ordering and unique recovery of the radii ratio from that observable, despite unknown crossing angle, are meaningful structural statements beyond the known total-volume integral. The exact nonanalytic correction at equal radii describes the singularity of intersecting boundary patches and is not a parameter substitution or unmotivated numerical slice.
